cards.title: Re-assessing never updates the dashboard (primary newest-wins)
cards.summary: DONE pending review (committed to master). Root-caused the dashboard-pinning bug found while live-smoking MV-14: partial-unique index assessments_primary_idx = UNIQUE(owner) WHERE is_primary allows one primary per owner; the dashboard reads the primary one; but claimAndBootstrapProfile ran a single unconditional promote (update is_primary=true .eq(id).is(is_primary,false)) and DISCARDED the returned {error}. On the 2nd+ claim the owner already has a primary, so the promote violated the index, the error was swallowed, the new row stayed is_primary=false, and the dashboard stayed pinned to the first assessment ever claimed (confirmed live: owner ece83f09 has 16 assessments, only the oldest is primary). Fix A (newest-wins): demote-then-promote as TWO sequential app-layer updates (business logic in Next.js, NOT a Postgres RPC — Codex suggested an RPC, overruled): (1) is_primary=false where owner=userId and is_primary=true, (2) is_primary=true where id=assessmentId; after the demote the owner has no primary so the promote can't trip the index. Both {error} results are now read + structured-logged ([claim] demote/promote ... failed) — no longer swallowed; misleading comment fixed; MV-14 lead-insert unchanged. Design call: LOG not throw (auth/callback has no try/catch — throwing would 500 an already-claimed user); residual demote-ok/promote-fail leaves a momentary no-primary state (logged), which MV-17 removes for the common path. No DB schema/scoring/golden change; F16 untouched. Gate green: typecheck/lint, full suite 1270/1270 (+2 TDD: newest-wins order+filters; failed-promote-is-logged). FOUNDER-OWED: live smoke (2nd assessment on an existing account → dashboard shows the new result; new row is_primary=true, old flipped false); existing pinned rows self-heal on next claim only (retro fix = prod write, founder-gated). Dossier: cards/MV-16-primary-assessment-newest-wins.md.
